note: One register per replaced test (the source spec's description lists them). Each claim is read through the flags the built variable carries, or the unresolved_flag error that withholds it when no summary row binds, and through the support issue the build reports. literal (test 1): the old rows both declared identifier false; here one row is sensitive and leaves the identifier blank and the other declares the identifier, so the variable is sensitive and an identifier only if both rows bind although neither row's endpoints name an edition it carries. The summary's non-flag fields and its target count are not visible in a build. incomplete (test 2): the old 'absent' endpoint is a blank cell, which the Unika reader reads as unknown, the same as the old empty one (scb_records.py `_cell_field`); neither variable binds, so both are withheld and one ambiguous_support_target cites both rows. identified-a and identified-b (test 3): VarID 9001 in two registers under two columns; Identifierare.csv declares it, so both are identifiers; undeclared is the twin without a declaration and is withheld. The old foreign-source leg has no build form: Registerinformation is the only target an SCB join declares (sources/scb_auxiliary.py). keyless (test 4): the blank-column row is an unknown_support_key error and the ABSENT row an unreferenced_support_record warning; the old blank-column target has no build form, since a delivered member without a column forms no variable (no_supported_states). conflicting (test 5): both 2003|2003 rows bind to old, whose identifier conflicts and is withheld alone (sensitivity is false in both rows), not OR-ed to true; new binds nothing. ratchet, unsensitive, conditional (test 6): sensitivity ratchets up across two rows of one variable. The old 'conditional' sensitivity value has no reader that produces it; Unika's conditional claim is its own KansligVariabelIbland column, which marks the variable sensitive. renumbered (test 9): each variable takes only the rows whose endpoints its own editions carry; the two equal rows stay together, so no ambiguous issue. shared (test 10): both variables carry 1997 and 2001, so the one row binds neither. unlisted (test 11): 1999 is no edition of old, so only its row is ambiguous and new still takes 2003|2003. Old literal variables (5, 6, edition labels 1989_old) are renumbered per register; the endpoints stay plain edition names. The issue `subject` names the support source and the literal key, which is how each support projection selects its register.
fails_if: any one of, per register: `SourceSupportBindings._dispositions` sends a key with one candidate to the discriminator, so literal's rows are ambiguous and literal/value is withheld (literal); `_endpoints` skips a blank endpoint instead of returning None, so incomplete's 2003| row binds to old (incomplete); the Identifierare join is dropped from `scb_support_joins` or keyed by register, so identified-a or -b is withheld (identified); a key-less summary row is grouped as unreferenced, or an unmatched one raised to an error (keyless); `reconcile_source_fields` ORs conflicting identifier claims, so conflicting/old is published as an identifier (conflicting); sensitivity stops ratcheting up, or `form_native_variable` ignores conditional_sensitivity, so ratchet or conditional is withheld or published non-sensitive (ratchet, conditional); `_discriminated` binds a partition to every candidate carrying its endpoints (`len(families) >= 1`), so shared/first takes the row (shared); a key with several candidates is reported ambiguous without consulting the endpoints, so renumbered's variables are withheld (renumbered); or `_discriminated` matches on the first endpoint alone, so unlisted/old takes 1997|1999 (unlisted)
